claims.explanation: GSK1070916 is a potent, long-residence-time inhibitor of Aurora B/C that kills proliferating tumor cells by disrupting mitosis and cytokinesis, so selectivity should track with dependence on Aurora B/C activity and high proliferative/mitotic rate rather than with any single lineage. Because Aurora B inhibition is most toxic when cells must transit mitosis, features that increase mitotic drive or Aurora B dependence (e.g., MYC/MYCN amplification, high AURKB expression, RB1 loss, TP53 loss) should sensitize, while features that reduce proliferation or engage G1 arrest (e.g., intact RB, EGFR-driven indolent lines, high CDKN2A/p21) should protect. Loss of p53 checkpoint allows mitotic catastrophe/polyploidy after Aurora B inhibition
RB loss increases mitotic entry and dependence on Aurora B-driven division
MYC-driven proliferation increases mitotic rate and Aurora B dependence
MYCN amplification drives rapid cycling and mitotic vulnerability
CDKN2A loss releases G1/S restraint, increasing cells in mitosis
Cyclin D1 overexpression promotes cell-cycle progression and mitotic entry
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006) are relatively resistant, likely slower cycling/oncogene-addicted
STK11/LKB1 loss associates with resistance in several listed lines
PTEN loss appears enriched in less-affected lines, possibly via reduced mitotic stress
BRAF-mutant lines (G361, MDAMB361, MFE319) are among least affected
CTNNB1-mutant lines (U2OS, LXF289, JHUEM2) appear among sensitive lines

raw.explanation: GSK1070916 is a potent, long-residence-time inhibitor of Aurora B/C that kills proliferating tumor cells by disrupting mitosis and cytokinesis, so selectivity should track with dependence on Aurora B/C activity and high proliferative/mitotic rate rather than with any single lineage. Because Aurora B inhibition is most toxic when cells must transit mitosis, features that increase mitotic drive or Aurora B dependence (e.g., MYC/MYCN amplification, high AURKB expression, RB1 loss, TP53 loss) should sensitize, while features that reduce proliferation or engage G1 arrest (e.g., intact RB, EGFR-driven indolent lines, high CDKN2A/p21) should protect. The observed sensitive lines are enriched for TP53 mutation and other proliferative/checkpoint-defective alterations, whereas several resistant lines are known to be relatively slow-growing or arrest-prone.
